reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion, date adjustment and holiday matching, but the range handler independently implements the daily occurrence policy already added to getNextDate.

duplication.why: Daily weekend and holiday exclusion is repeated in getNextDate and getDatesInRange instead of being defined once for all occurrence consumers.

placement.why: Holiday matching and adjustment belong in shared/schedules.ts, but the server handler also owns scheduling policy that should live alongside those shared definitions.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, configuration field and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate daily exclusion, date adjustment and configuration forwarding across multiple paths rather than update one shared occurrence policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts:getDatesInRange locally decides daily exclusion and passes config.skipWeekend && !daily to getScheduleDate, paralleling shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate instead of sharing that decision.

disguised_duplication.where: The daily non-working-day policy appears as a retrying while loop in getNextDate and a filtering continue in getDatesInRange, with both callers disabling adjustment for daily schedules.

abstraction_drift.where: A holidays parameter is added to getScheduleDate and getScheduleDateString; getNextDate adds daily exclusion and skipped-occurrence exhaustion branches; getDatesInRange independently implements daily exclusion, while getUpcomingDates retains its separate adjustment pipeline.
